summary: James Sutherland Cotton (1847–1918) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Magdalen College School, Brighton College, Winchester College, and Trinity College, Oxford, and later held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge from 1871 to 1874.

James Tod (1782–1835) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts with the East India Company from circa 1799 to 1823 and served as Librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1824 to 1835.
James W. Benson is an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at Harvard University as Assistant Professor in Sanskrit (attested 1999–2003) and at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

James W. Heisig is a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Nanzan University and the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (serving as director 1991–2001), and visited Pompeu Fabra University.
James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who founded the Columbia Zen Center. He served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

James Wilson Bright (1852–1926) was a linguist who studied at Lafayette College and Johns Hopkins University. He held positions at Cornell University around 1885 and at Johns Hopkins University from circa 1885 to 1924.
Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé (1813–1899) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Thekchok Dorje.

Jamie Hubbard works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held a professorship at Smith College (attested 2016).

Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1972–1979) and served as a wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1979–2004, attested 2005).
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.
Jampa Samten works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, serving as Director (attested 1991) and Professor (attested 2015).

Jampa Tegchok (1930–2014) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Sera Monastery. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1982), Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993), and the Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Jan C. Heesterman (1925–2014) was an Indology scholar who held a post at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990, where he was attested as Professor in 2014.
Jan Chozen Bays is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada, and served as abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery around 2002.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).

Jan Gonda (1905–1991) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht University (PhD under Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff) and Leiden University. He held chairs and posts at Utrecht University and the University of Chicago.

Jan Jaworski (1903–1945) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw from circa 1923 to 1930, studying under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.
Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889–1954) was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University (~1907–1911). He subsequently held academic posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1930 to 1954.

Jan N. Bremmer is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Bristol, later holding posts at Utrecht University (~1974–1990) and the University of Groningen (~1990–2009).

Jan Nattier is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Central Asian studies who studied at Indiana University and Harvard. She has held professorships at Macalester College, Indiana University, Soka University, and the University of Hawaii, among other institutions.
